'''Stanley Osher''' (born April 24, 1942) is an American mathematician, known for his many contributions in [[shock capturing]], [[level-set method]]s, and [[partial differential equation|PDE]]-based methods in [[computer vision]] and [[image processing]]. Osher is a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), Director of Special Projects in the [[Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics]] (IPAM) and member of the California NanoSystems Institute (CNSI) at UCLA.

==Education and career==
Osher received a bachelor's degree from [[Brooklyn College]] in 1962. He continued his studies at [[New York University]], where he received a master's degree in 1964<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sjo/oshercv.doc|title=Curriculum vitae|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref> and completed his Ph.D. in 1966.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|11645}}</ref>

After two years working at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratories]], he joined the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as an assistant professor of mathematics in 1968. He moved to [[Stony Brook University]] as an associate professor in 1970, and there was promoted to full professor in 1975. He moved again to the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] Department of Mathematics in 1977.<ref name=cv/>

He co-founded a spinoff company, Cognitech, in 1988, and remained affiliated with Cognitech until 1995.<ref name=cv/>

==Recognition==
Osher was a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Fellow]] in 1971,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cies.org/schlr_directories/ |title=Fulbright Scholar Directories |website=www.cies.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050305211620/http://www.cies.org/schlr_directories/ |archive-date=2005-03-05}}</ref> an [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Fellow]], 1972–1974<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sloan.org/fellowships|title=Sloan Research Fellowships &#124; Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|website=sloan.org|accessdate=December 17, 2021}}</ref> an SERC Fellow in England in 1982, and a US-Israel BSF Fellow in 1986.<ref name=cv/>

He was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2005,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/stanley-joel-osher-mezais/|title=Stanley Joel Osher|work=Member directory|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref> to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2009,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/stanley-j-osher|title=Stanley J. Osher|work=Member directory|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref> and to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nae.edu/178165/Dr-Stanley-Joel-Osher|title=Dr. Stanley Joel Osher|work=Members directory|publisher=National Academy of Engineering|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref> He was named as a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2009,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/fellows-program|title=Fellows Program &#124; SIAM|website=www.siam.org|accessdate=December 17, 2021}}</ref> and of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved March 20, 2013.</ref>

He is a 1992 recipient of the [[NASA]] Public Service Group Achievement Award,<ref name=cv/> the 2002 recipient of the Computational Mechanics Award of the Japan Society of Mechanical Engineering,<ref name=cv/> the 2003 recipient of the [[International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics|ICIAM]] Pioneer Prize,<ref name="auto"/> the 2005 recipient of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] Kleinman Prize,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/ralph-e-kleinman-prize|title=Ralph E. Kleinman Prize|website=SIAM|accessdate=December 17, 2021}}</ref> the 2007 recipient of the Computational and Applied Sciences Award of the United States Association for Computational Mechanics,<ref name=gauss/> and the 2007 recipient of the International Cooperation Award, given at the [[International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|department=Mathematics People|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200804/tx080400509p.pdf|title=Awards Presented at 2007 ICCM|page=509|date=April 2008|volume=55|issue=4}}</ref> He received the 2013 John von Neumann Lecture prize from [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/john-von-neumann-prize|title=John von Neumann Prize|website=SIAM|accessdate=December 17, 2021}}</ref> the 2014 [[Carl Friedrich Gauss Prize]],<ref name=gauss>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201410/rnoti-p1233.pdf|title=2014 Gauss Prize Awarded|pages=1233–1235|date=November 2014|volume=61|issue=10}}</ref> and the 2016 William Benter Prize in Applied Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cityu.edu.hk/rcms/WBP/|title=William Benter Prize in Applied Mathematics|website=www.cityu.edu.hk|accessdate=December 17, 2021}}</ref> 

He has honorary doctorates from [[École Normale Supérieure de Cachan|ENS Cachan]] in France in 2006<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ens-paris-saclay.fr/en/stanley-osher|title=Stanley Osher|publisher=ENS Paris Saclay|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref> and from [[Hong Kong Baptist University]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sci.hkbu.edu.hk/honorary-doctorate?lang=en|title=Honorary doctorate|publisher=Hong Kong Baptist University|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref> He was a plenary speaker at the 2010 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref name="auto">{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]}}</ref>
